purpose: External reference lists of London's major attractions, used by scripts/audit-attractions.mjs to answer 'what are we missing?' with a list rather than a guess.
why: Every research pass in the playbook starts from an editorial list - Time Out, The Infatuation, a cuisine guide. That finds what critics write about and structurally cannot find what they do not cover. This file is the opposite: a register of what is objectively big, ranked by visitor numbers or named by the official tourist board, so coverage can be measured against reality instead of against taste.

lists.name: ALVA / Wikipedia most-visited UK attractions (London entries)
lists.note: Ranked by audited visitor numbers for 2025. ALVA is the Association of Leading Visitor Attractions; these are the hard numbers, not an opinion.

lists.name: Paid-ticket landmarks and family attractions
lists.source: visitlondon.com top attractions; Merlin Entertainments London estate; commonly-cited visitor lists
lists.note: ALVA members are mostly free museums and heritage sites, so its table under-represents paid attractions and anything aimed at children - which is exactly the gap that let Babylon Park sit unlisted. These are the names a first-time visitor asks about.

lists.statusNote: DEFERRED BY DECISION, NOT MISSED. These sit outside London and need a decision about how the sheet represents somewhere you take a train to for the day - the geography table, the area guides and the Zone/District model all assume a London location. Recorded here so the audit does not keep re-reporting them as gaps and so they are not lost. Revisit when out-of-London day trips get their own treatment.
